## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Cūḷarathavimānavatthu* (Vv 63, also referenced as Vv 5.13) is a canonical text belonging to the *Vimānavatthu* collection [SuttaCentral; Radich 2007]. It recounts the story of Prince Sujāta, who renounced household life for the forest and was ordained into the holy life by the arahant Mahā-Kaccāna [Radich 2007]. Perceiving that the prince had only five months left to live, Mahā-Kaccāna urged him to generate merit; by learning the Dhamma and transforming his conduct prior to death, the prince secured a celestial rebirth [SuttaCentral; Radich 2007].
SuttaCentral records a passage-level parallel to the text in the *Kaṇhapetavatthu* (Pv 18) [SuttaCentral]. In agreement with this, text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus identifies close correspondences between verses §15.1–18.4 of the text and Pv 18 (§11.4–15.4), as well as significant reuse across the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, *Vessantarajātaka* (Ja 547), *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalīvimānavatthu* (Vv 83), *Nandakapetavatthu* (Pv 38), and *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalīpetavatthu* (Pv 17) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns several verses with cross-language parallels, including the Sanskrit and Tibetan *Udānavarga* traditions, the *Āryānityatāsūtra*, and discourses in the Chinese *Ekottarika-āgama* (T 125) [DharmaNexus].
